text: Before promising installs, test network (curl github.com, pip download). If blocked, say so and ask the user to enable network access in settings; never pretend to install.
Verify the kit is complete before planning (mix.py, toonbase.js, vendored three.js, Chromium). Missing pieces must be rebuilt or fetched, not assumed.
Render in ~12 s chunks to .mkv with auto-retry (RESUME=1), then concat. One long render process can die and leave a corrupt file.
CPU-only box (SwiftShader): ~2.5 s/frame at full res. Use half internal scale for drafts; final must still be real 30 fps (render 30; only double frames if stills show no ghosting).
Render and LOOK at mid-shot stills (contact sheet) before the full render. Fix framing/mirrored text first.
Final mix integrated loudness -14 LUFS (reference measured -14.2), true peak <= -1 dBTP. Music well under voice (about -14 dB), SFX short and never louder than voice peaks.
Never synthesize fake narration (espeak/sine). Voice comes from the user's file. Music/SFX are synthesized or from licensed files only.
Every shot start gets a transition sound matched to the camera move (whoosh up for push-in, down for pull-out), plus an impact/pop on each fx.
Ask for the original script with the audio. ASR of dialect (Arabic/Spanish) is unreliable; captions must be corrected from the script.
Captions: 1-3 words at a time, bold white with thick black outline, centered at ~78% of frame height, synced to speech. Burn with ffmpeg ass AFTER render, not inside the 3D engine.

Arabic needs a font with Arabic glyphs and libass shaping (Lalezar for the zach-d-films look; Noto Sans Arabic Bold as fallback). Never use a Latin-only font. Check a rendered frame for broken/disconnected letters.
Parakeet is English-only. For Arabic use Whisper multilingual (sherpa-onnx release models if Hugging Face is blocked). Without ASR, align the script to silence gaps (tools/timing_ar.py).
Reference style: ONE continuous 3D world with a never-stationary camera (zoom in/out, orbit, crane). No hard cuts; blend each shot's start pose from the previous shot's end pose.
A new visual idea every 1.5-3 s; never hold a shot >4.5 s without a new prop, annotation or camera phase.
Do not reuse the same shot twice. If the library lacks a prop for the sentence, BUILD a new prop (do not loop an old shot).
Explain with diegetic annotations: glowing arrows, dimension lines, shockwave rings, highlight pulses on the object being discussed.
Visual DNA: blue gradient studio void, white blueprint grid floor, soft light shaft, textured soil/diorama block with cross-section, 3D props, billboard cutout actors.
At the story pivot ('but the question is...') do a short fade through black (0.2-0.4 s) to reset attention.
3 hard cuts, reference style has none. Blend camera continuously between shots.
Strip trailing punctuation from caption words (RTL flips ':' to the wrong side; reference captions have none).
Write the script with | at every real pause so phrases == speech segments; timing_ar.py then anchors exactly. Check 'EXACT segment match' in its output.
9:16 frame => horizontal FOV is narrow. Camera dist must be >= ~1.4x the object width or it gets cropped; check stills for cropping.
Particles that pass within ~1.5 m of the camera become huge and pop. Skip them (z<1.5) and cap radius.

soft3d (CPU) output is flat-shaded: no textures, no billboard actors, no DOF/ink. Next upgrades: brick/soil textures, hen/person cutouts, soft shadows, annotation labels, richer props. When Chromium+three.js are available use engine/main.js instead.
Camera blend between shots must start slowly (smoothstep over 18 frames); easeOut over 10 frames caused near hard cuts flagged by postmortem.

User feedback on malqaf-v1: liked it, but wants MORE EXPRESSIVE graphics next time. Add: textured props (brick/soil), living actors (people/animals cutouts with idle motion), temperature/heat visual language (color-graded heat vs cool, shimmer, thermometer/gauge annotations), close-up inserts on the key mechanism, labeled callouts, dramatic lighting and slow-mo on the payoff.
EVERY video ends with the spoken CTA 'لو استفدت، اعمل لايك وتابع صفحة «وسّع مخك»... عشان مخك يوسع!', a final end-card shot (fx outro) and the big gold brand text 'وسّع مخك' (captions.py --brand).
First spoken sentence must be a curiosity hook (paradox/question/surprise) with no setup.
Page name is «وسّع مخك» (Wasa3 Mokhak). Use it in CTA, brand text, titles and descriptions.
When two things move (car + wave), use a dynamic focus on their midpoint so both stay in frame; check in stills.
For burst/cutaway events aim the camera (azimuth) at the OPEN side or the damage is invisible (tank burst needed az~80).
Topic props live in kit/tools/scenes/<topic>.py (register(PROPS,FOCUS,helpers,HOOKS)); timeline 'scene' key loads them. Reuse street/brick/window/car/gauge/blueprint builders from scenes/molasses.py.
Show key numbers as gold ASS callouts (captions.py --callouts) + a gauge dial for speeds; it makes facts visible.
For stories with deaths: sober colour grade (desaturate/dim), no victims shown, keep it short; user still gets the facts.
Use shot 'grade' {sat,bright,tint} to carry mood (sober grey-blue vs warm amber smell); it blends over 14 frames.
3 repeated shot segment(s). Build new props/views per sentence; never loop a shot.
storyboard.py must pass every per-shot field the renderer reads (grade, bg); it silently dropped them before, so mood grading was not applied in molasses-v1.
Dissolve 24 frames between different worlds (roof<->space); a 14-frame blend still registered as a hard cut in postmortem.
Space shots: keep gradient fixed and roll only the star layer by camera yaw/pitch (rolling the whole image creates a seam); vary camera angles or postmortem flags dark scenes as repeats.
Single tool calls time out at 300 s and background jobs die with the call: render in the foreground (about 0.13 s/frame) and finish in a separate call.
When the narrator pauses between phrases, split the script with | at EVERY pause (20 segments here) so timing_ar reports EXACT match.
In a new chat use kit/tools/build.sh (check, stills, render k n, finish) instead of calling tools by hand; it keeps every call under 300 s.

Optional add-on JDhruv14/line-art-animation (MIT): read kit/references/line-art-animation.md; install with kit/tools/install_lineart.sh when network works. Borrow: planted-foot gait solver, spring/pendulum secondary motion, day/night palette, 'show one figure first' rule.
